minutes.headline: Parks Commission agreed to pursue FY24 capital requests for McNally and Northfield surveys and push for Marshall Park engineering funding.
minutes.summary: The commission heard DPW and recreation updates, with sharp criticism of the recreation director over low registration for a youth sports program and undercharged swim lessons. It then set FY24 capital priorities, discussed seeking Marshall Park engineering money at the November special town meeting, and agreed on edits to the Marshall Park survey RFP. No formal vote beyond minutes and adjournment was recorded.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment from the public; none was offered.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the June 15th meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The recreation director read out pass sales by category.
Asked for total revenue, the director first gave one figure then corrected to a total for passes.
A member said a family was charged for only one child and several children may not have been charged; revenue goes to a revolving account under the commission.
Members confirmed the minimum dollar amount for a capital project is believed to be set in the financial policies.
Money left in the DPW parks line was said to be earmarked for the beach building, but the repair estimate was higher; it may flow back to free cash.
The chair wants engineering funded at the November special town meeting using free cash; a member cautioned about taxpayer pushback.
ARPA funds must be committed by 2024 and spent by the end of 2026; a large share may be earmarked for Marshall Park.
A member described a federal program mixing grants and low-interest loans for septic or sewer work.
A donation from a farm to the open space committee will pay for a title search on Stump Cove.

decisions.decision: FY24 capital requests to pursue: a survey of Northfield park and a survey plus conceptual design of McNally Park; Fitzgerald, Veterans Park and basketball court treated as care and maintenance.
Chair to request a meeting with the town manager about the two capital projects and the Marshall Park next phase; no vote needed.
Chair to ask the town manager about funding Marshall Park engineering at the November town meeting; if she declines, the commission decides at its next meeting whether to file a citizen's petition.
Commission asks the town manager to remove tree references and wedge outcropping detail from the Marshall Park survey RFP unless a compelling reason exists; a member will draft the email.
Wetland flagging to cover the whole park including around Marshall Pond, by a volunteer wetland scientist; no formal vote.
Recreation director asked to export and send the sales data for an audit.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission chose to pursue two FY24 capital requests: a survey of Northfield park and a survey with conceptual design for McNally Park.
The chair will ask the town manager about funding Marshall Park engineering at the November town meeting, and the commission will weigh a citizen's petition if she declines.
The commission asked the town manager to strip tree references and wedge outcropping detail from the Marshall Park survey RFP, with no formal vote.
The recreation director was asked to export sales data for an audit after a member said swim lessons may have been undercharged.
The only formal votes recorded were adjournment and, as captioned, a motion on the June minutes; the next meeting moved to September 14.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park engineering money, if sought at the November special town meeting from free cash, would be a vote residents are asked to take, and funds tied to ARPA have committed-by and spent-by deadlines.
The audit request touches swim lesson and beach revenue that goes into a revolving account under the commission, so how fees were charged affects what that account holds.
watch_next: Next Parks Commission meeting, moved to September 14, where the commission decides whether to file a citizen's petition if the town manager declines Marshall Park engineering funding.
The November special town meeting warrant, for any Marshall Park engineering article.
